chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The testimony of the Muslims is accepted over all the people of the religions, and the testimony of the people of the Dhimma is not accepted against the Muslims.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Dhimma (non-Muslims living under Muslim protection)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمِلَلِ: People of the religions (plural of millah, referring to various religious communities)

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of non-Muslims accepted against Muslims in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the asymmetry in legal testimony (shahada) within Shia jurisprudence, affirming that Muslim testimony is universally accepted against non-Muslims, while the reverse is not permitted. This ruling reflects the classical fiqh principle of 'adalat al-Muslim' (justice of the Muslim), distinguishing between Ahl al-Milal (polytheists/other faiths) and Ahl al-Dhimma (specifically Jews and Christians) in the context of civil and criminal courts. It underscores the theological and legal hierarchy where the integrity of a Muslim's witness is considered superior in mixed-religion disputes.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

The testimony of the Muslims would be accepted over the entirety of the people of (other) religions, and the testimony of the people under the responsibility (Ahl Al-Zimma) is not allowed against the Muslims’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu ‘ Ubaydah who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
testimony of Muslims is admissible against the people of all other nations. The testimony of taxpayers is not admissible against Muslims.”’
